rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked every pronoun/demonstrative/definite-noun across all 9 chunks in order (re-walked after the two diff edits at lines 16 and 76 — neither touches a referent). Closest-to-violating: chunk 1 line 22 'The curated security skills install when you extract the bundle.' — 'the bundle' is not named anywhere earlier in the file; the tarball is first named at chunk 4 (line 45, `ae101-content.tar.gz`) and 'the bundle' as a term first appears in chunk 5's own header (line 51). Stays inside: this is an aside, not an instruction the reader must act on at this slide — the verb 'extract' itself supplies the needed gist (a downloaded package you'll unpack later), so a first-time reader is not stranded mid-sentence, only mildly previewed-forward, which the rule's own chunk-0-lede carve-out treats as normal preview behaviour elsewhere in this same file (line 7). No other candidate found: chunk 3 line 40 'the repo you just picked' resolves to chunk 2 (sequential, fine); chunk 6 line 66 'the candidate-bug screen' resolves to chunk 6 line 62 'the bug screen' (in-chunk); chunk 8 line 80 'The bug you picked' resolves to chunk 6's bug-screen (session-artifact carve-out, backward same-file).

Two off-file links, both named not located: chunk 2 line 34 '[build one from zero](trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/build-a-project-from-zero.md)' names the destination in the link text itself; chunk 7 line 76 'Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](...)' names author and title in the same sentence (the line's diff edit only moved a bold span, the naming is untouched). Neither points at another file by position ('the opening lecture said'). No cross-file positional callback found anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The only backward-pointing 'the X you did' phrasing is chunk 8 line 80 'The bug you picked' — the pick happens in this same file's chunk 6, an earlier slide, not a cross-file beat, so it is same-file sequential resolution (rule 1's domain) rather than the cross-beat pattern rule 3 targets. No reference in the body points at a prior module's exercise/lecture beat (this file precedes Module 1; there is no prior module to reference). N/A-shaped in substance, scored PASS since the rule's own failure mode (a dead beat reference) is absent, not merely inapplicable.

Thinnest chunk by word count (per `check-slide-size.js --report`, re-run this pass) is chunk 4 '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' at 17 words, but it still carries two self-standing instructions (fetch the tarball via the prompt; manual-download fallback link) — not a bare wait-state or context-dependent bullet. Every other chunk carries substantially more standalone content. No orphan found.

Checked all 8 headers against their own chunk content. Closest-to-violating: chunk 4 '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' (line 43) — the chunk's own content (line 45) only asks the student to fetch `ae101-content.tar.gz`, which becomes a folder only after chunk 5's extraction. Stays inside: nothing in the chunk contradicts the header ('folder' names the eventual, well-understood outcome of the download step in this two-step download+extract pair, and chunk 5's own header 'Extract the bundle' makes the split explicit) — no false claim, just an anticipatory label. Every other header matches its content exactly (e.g. 'Bring to Module 1' vs. the bug + trick reminder it contains).

Checked all 5 sub-items across all 9 chunks including both diff-touched lines (16, 76): no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative (nothing like 'one of the most useful moves in the training' — value-prop-leak sub-item clean); no number-plus-own-retraction (the runtime/time figures sit in the maintainer block, below the cut, exempt; none in the body retract themselves); no abstraction-noun stack; no empty-leg verb triplet. Clean across the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped the expanded body (prompt blocks included, since `has_prompt_blocks: true`) for repo/maintainer vocabulary (compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, surface-as-noun, firing, Connections) — zero hits. 'Plan mode' (chunk 1 line 16) is a real Claude Code product feature, ordinary to the engineer audience, not repo-internal dialect. 'Session' widget label (chunk 3 line 38) is the canonical architecture-mandated widget name, same status as '## Big Idea'. The two extracted prompt blocks (chunks 4, 5, 6) use plain engineering vocabulary (screen, candidate, trivial, tarball) throughout — no dialect terms found there either.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Diff-verified fix: `git diff e11bbeb4..HEAD` shows chunk 7 line 76 changed from bolding the whole span '**Read: Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](...)**' (flagged REVISE in the prior instance at this file's earlier pin) to bolding only '**Read:**', leaving 'Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Oct/7/vibe-engineering/) (October 2025)' plain. Current line 76 carries exactly one bolded element, 1 word, well under the ≲5-word handle cap and inside the ≤1-per-slide budget — and it is the literal shape the compendium names as correct: 'bold the mode word alone (`**Read:**`, `**Watch:**`) and leave the title plain.' Chunk 1's four task-size bullet bolds ('Trivial bug', 'A small multi-file task', 'A small feature', 'A bigger piece', lines 15-18, unaffected by the diff at line 16 which only touched the plain-text tail) remain short (≤3-word) checklist-item handles distinguishing entries a reader scans to find their own task size — same protected shape as the reading-list/module-template exceptions, not flagged. No other chunk carries more than one bolded element. Clean across the file — no REVISE remaining.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 8 body headings are imperative ('Bring real work', 'Bring to Module 1') or numbered phase/step labels ('1. Pick THE repo' … '5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness') — the exercise-heading convention, consistent throughout, matching what this file actually is (a task walkthrough, not a lecture). No slide in this file is a law/consolidation moment where 'the header IS the teaching' — every chunk is logistics (bring X, pick Y, run Z) — so the claim requirement the rule's 2026-08-19 generalisation binds to law/consolidation slides is never triggered here. 'Pre-read before Module 1' and 'Bring to Module 1' both read as the explicit NOT-violation carve-out (catalogue entries / orientation-style labels), not mislabelled claims.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all three classes against every bullet/sentence in all 9 chunks, including the diff-touched line 16. (a) doctrine restatement — none found; the file has no lens/split/law re-announced after doing its work (prework has no doctrine to restate, it is pure logistics). (b) self-referential design commentary — none found; no sentence tells the student they are inside a pedagogy. (c) aphorism kicker — closest candidate is chunk 6 line 70 '*Small steer, small trick. A minute here, another there.*'; stays inside because it is concrete to the specific AskUserQuestion tip just given in the same chunk (lines 66-68), not a restatement of the header or of a `**The point:**`-style line, and at 7 words costs nothing it doesn't also earn as a light transition into the next chunk. Chunk 1 line 20 'Separate tasks off your backlog.' is an instruction (an action to take), not a doctrine restatement of the four bullets above it; the line-16 edit (dropping 'soon after') removes a redundant timing qualifier, it doesn't introduce one. No bullet meeting the 'carries nothing' bar found.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body (grepped for 'guess'/'predict'/'take a guess' — zero hits); prework has no live-demo beat to break.
